newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks sees higher sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks sees higher sales in 1997.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo's truck unit said on Friday that it saw higher sales in 1997 after sales slipped 17 percent in 1996 to 63,682 vehicles.

Volvo Trucks' chief executive Karl-Erik Trogen told Reuters in an interview in Brussels that he expected stronger sales even though he forecast slightly weaker markets in Europe and North America this year.
"The answer is yes," Trogen said when asked if Volvo truck was expecting sales to go up this year.
He could not give a more exact forecast.
"It is so market related," he said.
Trogen said that he expected Volvo Trucks to return to profit in South America this year after the market fell in 1995.
"I expect to be in black levels in 1997 in South America," Trogen said.
Asked what he thought of the different markets, Trogen said he thought Europe would be a strong market. But Volvo expected it would be a little weaker than in 1996.
In Europe. Volvo's truck unit delivered 35,030 trucks last year, which was little changed from 35,190 in 1995.
The North American market is expected to continue weakening over the year and Volvo Trucks could expect a drop of about 10 percent.
In North America Volvo sold 16,855 trucks last year which was a fall of 38 percent from a year earlier.
"The outside conditions will be a little more troublesome for us," Trogen said.
Volvo still hopes to increase its market share in North America which last year fell to about nine percent from earlier levels of about 12-13 percent.
"Our ambition, is to very, very quickly get back market share .... to 12-13 percent," he said.
